title: Hazel and the Alibi
premise: Beatrix Dravenmoor, concierge of the Saltmere Grand Hotel, has spent fifteen years cataloguing the town's secrets in a private ledger — including the disappearance of Hazel Vane, a chambermaid who vanished the night of the solstice tide. When Hazel's diary surfaces in a donated suitcase with entries written after her disappearance, Beatrix realizes someone has been keeping Hazel alive on paper — or hiding her. Following the diary's coded references to her own ledger, Beatrix uncovers that the hotel's beloved owner used the tide caves to smuggle people out of dangerous marriages and debts, and that Hazel chose to disappear into that network rather than be silenced as a witness. The climax comes at the next solstice tide, when Beatrix trades her fifteen years of filed secrets for Hazel's freedom, exposing the one crime the network couldn't absolve; in the end, Hazel returns not as a missing person but as the new keeper of the ledger, and Beatrix finally stops watching other people's lives from behind the front desk.
about_author: Lena Eastwick is the pen name of a former night-shift receptionist who swears every hotel lobby is a confession booth with better lighting. She writes mysteries about women who notice too much and are paid too little.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Small Sins
chapters.summary: POV: Beatrix. A quiet October morning at the Saltmere Grand establishes Beatrix's ritual: she files guests' secrets — affairs, forged checks, whispered threats — in a coded ledger only she can read. The fifteenth anniversary of Hazel Vane's disappearance passes unmarked by the town. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as competence; Beatrix believes observation is a substitute for living.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: POV: Beatrix. A widow donates a suitcase of her late husband's effects; inside is Hazel's diary, its final entry dated nine days after she vanished — and written in a hand gone shakier, more frightened. Beatrix recognizes a phrase from her own ledger's code embedded in the text. Emotional beat: vertigo; the file she closed fifteen years ago just opened itself.

chapters.title: Room 214 Keeps Its Silence
chapters.summary: POV: Beatrix. She quietly investigates the suitcase's donor chain and finds the husband once stayed at the hotel the week Hazel disappeared — in room 214, where the ledgers show an erased charge. The current owner, Edmund Saltmere, deflects her questions with practiced warmth. Emotional beat: first real fear; the hotel she trusts may be the crime scene.

chapters.title: What the Tide Takes Twice
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Beatrix and diary excerpts. The diary describes a hidden door beneath the boathouse and 'the ferryman who charges no fare.' Beatrix finds the door at low tide — and fresh boot prints going in. Someone else knows. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into purpose; she is no longer reading the mystery, she is inside it.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Fare
chapters.summary: POV: Beatrix. In the caves she discovers the truth of the network: for decades the hotel has spirited abused spouses and debtors out of Saltmere under new names — and Hazel was one of its couriers, not its victim. But the diary's later entries mention 'the one he wouldn't let leave.' Emotional beat: relief curdling into confusion; rescue and captivity share a doorway.

chapters.title: A Ledger Written in Two Hands
chapters.summary: POV: Beatrix, with a flashback chapter from Hazel's voice. Comparing the diary against her own fifteen-year ledger, Beatrix decodes a second, hidden column: payments. Someone was being paid to keep Hazel listed as dead. The handwriting matches Edmund's late father — and, faintly, Edmund's. Emotional beat: betrayal; the institution she gave her life to built its kindness on a lie.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Filed Secrets
chapters.summary: POV: Beatrix. Edmund confronts her, offering partnership: keep the secret, inherit the network, finally matter. He reveals the erased charge — Hazel witnessed a guest's murder by his father, and the network hid her to protect itself, paying her to stay gone. Emotional beat: temptation; Beatrix must weigh belonging against justice outside any courtroom.

chapters.title: The Solstice Register
chapters.summary: POV: Beatrix. Refusing the bargain, Beatrix prepares to expose everything but realizes the police will bury it — Edmund owns the town's goodwill. Instead she sends a coded message through the network itself, using the diary's cipher, addressed to the one address that never appears in any ledger. Emotional beat: resolve; she chooses the dangerous version of right over the safe version of wrong.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gives Back
chapters.summary: POV: Beatrix and Hazel. At the solstice tide, Hazel answers — alive, weathered, furious at being summoned. Confronted together, Edmund confesses his father's murder and his own fifteen years of complicity as Beatrix records every word in her ledger, the tide rising behind them like a witness. Emotional beat: catharsis; two keepers of secrets finally say one true thing aloud.

chapters.title: Concierge No Longer
chapters.summary: POV: Beatrix, closing with Hazel. Edmund faces the law he long evaded; the network, cleansed, needs new hands. Hazel takes over the ledger and offers Beatrix a place in the found family she unknowingly kept safe for fifteen years. Beatrix hands in her keys — then stays, not as staff, but as partner. Emotional beat: homecoming; the woman who watched everyone's life finally claims her own.
